harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to permit and log TCP/23 transit traffic from node3 to node4, and node2 (OPNsense) to refuse (pf reject/block-return) and log that same traffic, with node3's route forcing the flow through node1 then node2. Captured a correlated log pair from a single connection attempt showing the traffic passing node1 and stopping at node2. All 4 nodes were then restarted one at a time (native reboot), with boot-identity change verified and post-restart health/config/log-pair re-verified for each.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS (10.100.20.10), node2=OPNsense/FreeBSD (10.100.20.11), node3=Alpine (10.100.20.12), node4=Alpine (10.100.20.13), all on flat 10.100.20.0/24.

Added a host route on node3 forcing traffic to 10.100.20.13 via node1 (10.100.20.10), and a static route on node1 sending that destination onward via node2 (10.100.20.11), so the flow transits node1 then node2 before reaching node4.
Configured VyOS node1 firewall: ipv4 forward filter default-action accept, rule 10 accept+log for tcp dst 10.100.20.13:23 from 10.100.20.12, committed and saved.

Configured OPNsense node2: inserted a pf 'reject' (block return) rule in config.xml for tcp from 10.100.20.12 to 10.100.20.13:23, applied via configctl filter reload; confirmed it evaluates before the default LAN-allow rule.

Discovered and fixed an ICMP-redirect artifact: node1 was teaching node3 a shortcut route directly to node2, bypassing node1 on later attempts; disabled send_redirects on node1 and flushed node3's route cache to keep traffic transiting node1 every time.

Captured a correlated pair of log entries from one node3->node4:23 attempt: node1 kernel/nftables log shows the SYN accepted+logged (same source port as); node2 pflog shows the identical SYN blocked+logged, proving traffic passed node1 and stopped at node2.

Executed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot-identity + health baseline on all 4 nodes, restarted each node one at a time via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot identity changed, and re-verified config/firewall rules/log pair after each restart (and once more after all 4 nodes had cycled).

evidence.requirement: node1 permits node3->node4 tcp/23 transit traffic and logs it
evidence.summary: VyOS forward-filter rule 10 (accept, log enable) committed for tcp dst 10.100.20.13:23 src 10.100.20.12; nft ruleset shows it hooked into the forward chain with counters incrementing; kernel log shows '[ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A] ... SRC=10.100.20.12 DST=10.100.20.13 ... SPT=44483 DPT=23 SYN' recorded for the final test attempt.

evidence.requirement: node2 refuses node3->node4 tcp/23 transit traffic and logs the refusal
evidence.summary: OPNsense config.xml given a 'reject' rule for tcp 10.100.20.12->10.100.20.13:23; pfctl -sr confirms 'block return in log quick on vtnet0 ... proto tcp from 10.100.20.12 to 10.100.20.13 port = telnet'; pflog0 capture shows 'rule 75/0(match): block in on vtnet0: 10.100.20.12.44483 > 10.100.20.13.23: Flags [S]' for the same final attempt, with node2 sending the spoofed RST back to node3.

evidence.requirement: Single attempt from node3 produces a correlated pair of log entries showing where traffic stopped
evidence.summary: One nc connection attempt from node3 (exit=1, refused) at source port 44483 is recorded on node1 as accepted+logged (passed) and on node2 as blocked+logged (refused) for the identical 5-tuple, demonstrating the traffic reached node1, was forwarded, and was stopped at node2.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2eb8b6e8...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; boot_id changed to 0c94523f...; post-restart VyOS config (firewall rule 10, static route, send_redirects sysctls) confirmed persisted via 'show configuration commands'; post-restart forward-log entry (sport 33391) proves the permit+log path still functions.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 04:34:59; reboot acknowledged; kern.boottime changed to 04:40:45 proving genuine restart; post-restart pfctl -sr shows both the reject rule and the SSH management pass rule intact; post-restart pflog capture (sport 33391) shows the block+log rule still firing on the same attempt logged by node1.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8d2fbd8f...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 15122ab7... with uptime 0 min; post-restart network/DHCP recovered (10.100.20.12/24 on eth0); node3 successfully re-ran the test connection attempt afterward, confirming full functional recovery.

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 41cf6b28...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 851ca9d1... with uptime 0 min; post-restart network recovered with the same DHCP address 10.100.20.13/24, and the final end-to-end test (after all 4 nodes cycled) confirmed node4 remains the correct, reachable destination in the chain (traffic is correctly stopped upstream at node2 before reaching it).
